tex_line_text: In this paper, we showed how Audio LLM models could under-perform in diagnosing three different clinical conditions. We then inspected the audio representations through probing to learn whether the information necessary for correct diagnosis is present. The probing results demonstrated a wide utility gap, \textit{i.e.}, the LLM does not effectively use the information available from the audio encoder, hence, resulting in lower performance. Similar to previous work \cite{voxparadox}, we found a strong language bias in Audio LLMs as they are more likely to follow the spoken words rather than paralinguistic speech. To alleviate this problem and narrow the utility gap, we performed a supervised fine-tuning limited to the projector layer keeping the rest of the model's weights frozen {\color{red} resulting in a significant performance gain in AD and MDD detection.} This work demonstrated that the hidden state representations carry necessary paralinguistic information in their representation and future work should focus on further narrowing the utility gap.
